# BMS / DJMax Keysound Slicer UX audit (research snapshot 2026-09-18)

**Evidence discipline.** I found strong primary/first-hand evidence for Sayaslicer, Woslicer II/III, BMHelper/Mid2BMS workflow, sound-slicer, BMS limits and DJMAX key-sound behavior. I did **not** find a public PTSEQUENCER manual, a usable Woslicer issue tracker, or enough YouTube comment text to support claims about those products. “Not found” is reported rather than inferred.

## 1. Comparison table

| Tool | Workflow actually documented | Top 3 pain points / limits | Max slices / snap | Export method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sayaslicer** | Open audio; add markers; optionally import MIDI/clipboard; set offset/snap; preview; copy BMSE/iBMSC markers or keysound list; export keysounds; paste into BMSE/iBMSC. The README explicitly describes this feature set and shortcuts. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)) | It still materializes files at export; zero-cross can move markers and make iBMSC data unsafe; very large files over 2 GB fail/lag. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer), [Issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5)) | Arbitrary 1/1–1/192; no stated slice-count cap; BMSE clipboard rounds to nearest 192nd, while iBMSC supports arbitrary resolution. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)) | WAV/key-sound export; BMSE and iBMSC clipboard; keysound list/BMS append. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)) |
| **Woslicer II** | Load WAV; position cursor on waveform; change grid; add/remove markers; preview current segment; export all numbered WAVs; paste clipboard sequence into BMSE. Documented shortcuts are O/Z/C, arrows, Q/W, P/Enter and M. ([FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)) | Keyboard-centric and legacy; input WAV incompatibility/crashes are reported, especially 24/32-bit or Studio One output; end/tail adjustment is left to the maker. ([Mid2BMS wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer), [FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)) | Guide says default 1/16 and Q/W change grid; no published max. ([FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)) | Batch numbered WAVs (“総出力”/M), then BMSE clipboard. ([FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)) |
| **Woslicer III** | Drag WAV; click waveform/grid to add markers (right-click removes); optionally copy cut positions from BMHelper and paste via clipboard; set BPM; batch export; copy sequence to BMSE. ([Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)) | Multi-program “clipboard ceremony”; file-name/focus quirks can disable output; pop-noise/incorrect tail behavior from the fade/extension algorithm; unsupported WAVs may crash. ([Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [Qiita investigation](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71), [Mid2BMS wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer)) | No numeric maximum published in the guides; grid density is selectable but no denominator is stated. | Batch WAV files plus clipboard sequence/definitions for BMSE. ([Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) |
| **BMHelper + Mid2BMS** | BMHelper imports MIDI, “new split” groups notes, adjusts minimum interval and value-difference tolerance, exports MIDI; DAW renders it; Woslicer cuts it; BMHelper copies positions and sequence; BMSE receives definitions/sequence. Mid2BMS is described as combining MIDI processing and slicing, but the author does not use it. ([Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html)) | Requires DAW round-trip; reverb/send must be removed before render or tails complicate splitting; BMSE drag order and starting selection must exactly match file order; author says Mid2BMS did not fit their workflow. ([Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) | No max/snap cap documented in fetched sources. | MIDI/audio intermediary, then WAV + copied BMS definitions/sequence. ([Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) |
| **PTSEQUENCER** | No sufficiently detailed public workflow source was found in this run. | The NamuWiki article attributes a 1,023 key-sound limit to the DJMAX pattern tool and says DPC 2025 raised it to 2,047, but this is secondary and not a PTSEQUENCER manual. ([NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)) | 1,023 historically / 2,047 reported for DPC 2025; no snap documentation found. ([NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)) | Not verified. |
| **dtinth sound-slicer** | Keep original project files and TXT in a parent folder; rendered numbered WAVs and BMS live in `wav`; tool reads TXT, slices WAV, and generates BMx clipboard data. Rhythmic mode makes one slice per event; melodic mode groups/reuses equivalent notes. ([README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) | Rhythmic mode can create 1,000 slices for 1,000 MIDI notes and slight gaps; both modes do not support BPM changes; melodic mode requires re-rendering a generated MIDI through an audio application. ([README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) | No max/snap documented. | Numbered WAVs + BMS clipboard. ([README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) |

## 2. Problem inventory

### Timeline / editing

- **P1 — No unified chart/audio view.** The documented workflow repeatedly switches BMHelper → DAW → Woslicer → BMSE, with clipboard transfers between them; Woslicer itself exposes waveform markers, not the target editor’s note chart. ([Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))
- **P1 — Grid is BPM-dependent and fragile.** Woslicer requires the user to set BPM before output; sound-slicer explicitly does not support BPM changes; Sayaslicer calls its partial BPM-change support “a bit hackish” and lists proper BPM/grid support as planned. ([Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer))
- **P0 — Boundary audio can be wrong.** A controlled Qiita analysis found Woslicer III can append reversed/inverted audio and insert a zero sample; the author concludes fade-before-cut shortens audio, fade-after-cut can leak the next sound, and the artifact can produce a pop. ([Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71))
- **P1 — Tail policy is not obvious/safe.** The Woslicer tutorial tells users to adjust the end and warns that a one-minute key sound can make a BMS fail “keyless BMS” checks; BMHelper’s minimum interval is a manual workaround for releases/reverb. ([FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))

### Interface / workflow

- **P0 — Export ceremony and fragile hand-offs.** Users must prepare an empty BMS, maintain open tools, copy cut positions, focus a black panel to make a file name appear, batch-export, then paste definitions/sequence at the correct starting location. ([Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html))
- **P1 — File-management burden.** The legacy pattern is one numbered WAV per segment in a `wav` folder; BMSE definitions depend on Explorer ordering and the selected starting row. ([sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer), [Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))
- **P1 — Silent placement/definition errors are easy.** Guides warn to align the first selected BMSE definition and sequence position, and to preserve file ordering; a wrong starting point can produce a plausible but wrong chart. ([Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))
- **P2 — Discoverability trades off with speed.** Woslicer II’s dense shortcut set is efficient for experts (Z, Q/W, P, M), while Woslicer III adds mouse placement; the documented UX still requires memorizing legacy keys. ([FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))

### Settings / compatibility

- **P0 — Format rejection becomes a crash/workaround.** The Woslicer wiki reports unreadable WAVs and forced exits, especially Studio One output and 24/32-bit WAV; users are told to round-trip through SoundEngine Free/Audacity. ([Mid2BMS wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer))
- **P1 — Zero-crossing is not a free improvement.** Sayaslicer warns that zero-cross markers move timing and may break iBMSC clipboard data; it recommends BMSE clipboard rounding when pasted chart data is missing or the game mode changes. ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer))
- **P1 — Resolution/encoding overflow.** Traditional BMS used base-36 01–ZZ (1,295 usable values); the source reports BMSE’s 2024 pilot base-62 expansion to 3,843. Sayaslicer therefore offers BMSE base-62 toggle and separate iBMSC clipboard export, while BMSE clipboard rounds to 192nd. ([NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer))
- **P2 — Large source files.** Sayaslicer issue #5 reports >2 GB files lagging or becoming unusable/failing to load. A virtual-slice backend should still stream/seek safely rather than assume small exports. ([Issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5))

### Backend / playback model

- **P0 — Hard key-count/capacity constraints shape composition.** NamuWiki reports 255→2,047 limits in EZ2AC, DJMAX’s older 1,023 figure and a reported 2,047 update, and BMS 1,295 base-36 / 3,843 base-62 identifiers. It also documents older same-track sample interruption and BMS engines that restart the same sample. ([NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C))
- **P1 — Reuse is valuable but awkward.** sound-slicer’s melodic mode reduces 500 repeated bass notes to 10 reusable slices, while rhythmic mode emits 1,000 slices for 1,000 notes; the choice is currently a separate workflow mode. ([sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer))
- **P1 — Non-destructive editing is absent from documented legacy workflows.** All described Woslicer/sound-slicer paths export numbered files before BMSE import; Sayaslicer improves this with save/load projects and undo/redo but still has an explicit keysound export step. ([Woslicer guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer))
- **P1 — Key-sound playback semantics matter.** The source says DJMAX/TECHNIKA-era systems evolved from same-lane interruption to non-interfering playback in Technika 2, while BMS may restart same-number samples; the Studio slicer needs an explicit target playback mode, not just a WAV exporter. ([NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C))

## 3. What Sayaslicer did right vs Woslicer — keep these

**Keep from Sayaslicer:** arbitrary 1/1–1/192 snapping; offset; zero-crossing with an explicit warning; silent-tail threshold and fade; MIDI import; BMSE and iBMSC clipboard formats; base-62 toggle; project save/load; marker copy/paste; undo/redo; multilingual UI; and keyboard-layout-aware shortcuts. These directly address Woslicer’s format, clipboard and ergonomic gaps. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer))

**Keep from Woslicer:** fast keyboard navigation and preview/auto-advance; simple visual marker placement; direct BMHelper cut-position interchange; batch export; and Woslicer III’s mouse placement. Users’ guides call the MIDI+BMHelper route “very easy” because it groups repeated pitches and chords before slicing, while still retaining brute-force slicing for automation/non-MIDI material. ([Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html))

## 4. Top 10 recommendations for DJMax Studio slicer

1. **P0 — Make every slice virtual first.** Store `{sourceFile,startMs,endMs}` plus per-slice processing; export WAV/OGG only on finalize. This removes the numbered-file/import ceremony documented for Woslicer and sound-slicer. ([Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer))
2. **P0 — Add a dual timeline:** waveform/ruler below and live Studio chart preview above, with one playhead and bidirectional selection. Existing workflows split these views across Woslicer/BMSE and require clipboard hand-offs. ([Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))
3. **P0 — Use sample-accurate, previewable boundary processing.** Offer zero-cross on/off, click-safe crossfade, tail/reverb policy, and A/B preview; never silently reverse/invert or inject a sample. Woslicer’s documented pop artifact makes this a correctness feature. ([Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71))
4. **P0 — Add target modes BMS / RESPECT / TECHNIKA.** Validate identifiers and playback semantics per target; warn before exceeding BMS base-36/base-62 or DJMAX reported limits, and model TECHNIKA-style non-interruption explicitly. ([NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D음))
5. **P0 — Make “Import to Studio” round-trip atomic.** Slicer and chart should share one project ID; importing should create notes and references, not clipboard text or filename-order assumptions. ([Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer))
6. **P1 — Provide a Slice Library with Draft slice.** Show source, start/end, duration, reuse count, waveform thumbnail, and audible preview; allow dedupe/reuse like sound-slicer melodic mode without forcing a separate render. ([sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer))
7. **P1 — Make snap explicit and layered.** Offer 1/4…1/192, ms/sample mode, BPM-change-aware grid, offset, and a visible “unsnapped/zero-cross moved” badge. Sayaslicer proves users need arbitrary 192nd and need to know when zero-cross changes timing. ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer))
8. **P1 — Put per-slice Zero-X / Fade / Normalize beside global defaults.** Include sensitivity (default proposal 0.55), silent-tail threshold, fade length, and an audition button; preserve overrides through undo/redo. This directly addresses reverb-tail, fade, and pop-noise workarounds in the guides. ([Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer))
9. **P1 — Add guardrails and diagnostics.** Detect unsupported codecs/bit depths, huge files, overlapping/restarted notes, >limit identifiers, and suspicious silent/double placements; give a repair action rather than a crash or silent wrong paste. ([Mid2BMS wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%83%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer), [Issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5), [Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))
10. **P1 — Keep expert shortcuts, but make them discoverable.** Preserve Woslicer’s Z/Q/W/P/M muscle memory and Sayaslicer’s selection/marker undo model; add command search, shortcut overlay, auto-advance Grid/Beat/Off and configurable keymap. ([FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer))

### Evidence gaps

The Sayaslicer issues index showed no open issues in the fetched page, while search surfaced the closed/labelled Issue #5; therefore I cannot honestly provide a “top 10” issue summary. No usable public issue/discussion corpus for Woslicer II/III, no PTSEQUENCER manual, and no reliable YouTube comment corpus were found. The proposed UI values “1380×860”, sensitivity 0.55 and the exact auto-advance options are treated as product requirements to validate, not as observed existing-tool behavior.
